audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 2 Samuel chapter 20, first-pass draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for Sheba's secession, ten concubines' lifelong confinement after rape, Amasa's deadline, Joab's deceptive greeting and murder, corpse exposure, coerced troop loyalty, siege of Abel, wise woman's negotiation, collective city risk, Sheba's beheading, and forced-labor administration.

verses.restored: A worthless/rebellious man was there, named Sheba son of Bichri, a Benjaminite. He blew shofar and said, We have no share in David and no inheritance in son of Jesse. Each to his tents, Israel.

familiar.text: And there happened to be there a man of Belial, whose name was Sheba, the son of Bichri, a Benjamite: and he blew a trumpet, and said, We have no part in David, neither have we inheritance in the son of Jesse: every man to his tents, O Israel.

modern.text: Now a worthless man named Sheba son of Bichri, a Benjamite, happened to be there, and he blew the ram’s horn and shouted: “We have no share in David, no inheritance in Jesse’s son. Every man to his tent, O Israel!”

original.text: וְשָׁ֨ם נִקְרָ֜א אִ֣ישׁ בְּלִיַּ֗עַל וּשְׁמ֛וֹ שֶׁ֥בַע בֶּן בִּכְרִ֖י אִ֣ישׁ יְמִינִ֑י וַיִּתְקַ֣ע בַּשֹּׁפָ֗ר וַ֠יֹּאמֶר אֵֽין לָ֨נוּ חֵ֜לֶק בְּדָוִ֗ד וְלֹ֤א נַֽחֲלָה לָ֨נוּ֙ בְּבֶן יִשַׁ֔י אִ֥ישׁ לְאֹהָלָ֖יו יִשְׂרָאֵֽל

verses.restored: Every man of Israel went up from after David and followed Sheba son of Bichri, but men of Judah clung to their king from Jordan to Jerusalem.

familiar.text: So every man of Israel went up from after David, and followed Sheba the son of Bichri: but the men of Judah clave unto their king, from Jordan even to Jerusalem.

modern.text: So all the men of Israel deserted David to follow Sheba son of Bichri. But the men of Judah stayed by their king all the way from the Jordan to Jerusalem.

original.text: וַיַּ֜עַל כָּל אִ֤ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ מֵאַחֲרֵ֣י דָוִ֔ד אַחֲרֵ֖י שֶׁ֣בַע בֶּן בִּכְרִ֑י וְאִ֤ישׁ יְהוּדָה֙ דָּבְק֣וּ בְמַלְכָּ֔ם מִן הַיַּרְדֵּ֖ן וְעַד יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם

verses.restored: David came to his house at Jerusalem. King took ten women, concubines he left to guard house, placed them in guarded house, and sustained them, but did not come to them. They were confined until day of their death, living as widows.

familiar.text: And David came to his house at Jerusalem; and the king took the ten women his concubines, whom he had left to keep the house, and put them in ward, and fed them, but went not in unto them. So they were shut up unto the day of their death, living in widowhood.

modern.text: When David returned to his palace in Jerusalem, he took the ten concubines he had left to care for the palace, and he placed them in a house under guard. He provided for them, but he no longer slept with them. They were confined until the day of their death, living as widows.

original.text: וַיָּבֹ֨א דָוִ֣ד אֶל בֵּיתוֹ֮ יְרֽוּשָׁלִַם֒ וַיִּקַּ֣ח הַמֶּ֡לֶךְ אֵ֣ת עֶֽשֶׂר נָשִׁ֣ים פִּלַגְשִׁ֡ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר הִנִּיחַ֩ לִשְׁמֹ֨ר הַבַּ֜יִת וַֽיִּתְּנֵ֤ם בֵּית מִשְׁמֶ֨רֶת֙ וַֽיְכַלְכְּלֵ֔ם וַאֲלֵיהֶ֖ם לֹא בָ֑א וַתִּהְיֶ֧ינָה צְרֻר֛וֹת עַד י֥וֹם מֻתָ֖ן אַלְמְנ֥וּת חַיּֽוּת

verses.restored: King said to Amasa, Summon men of Judah for me within three days, and you stand here.

familiar.text: Then said the king to Amasa, Assemble me the men of Judah within three days, and be thou here present.

modern.text: Then the king said to Amasa, “Summon the men of Judah to come to me within three days, and be here yourself.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ אֶל עֲמָשָׂ֔א הַזְעֶק לִ֥י אֶת אִישׁ יְהוּדָ֖ה שְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת יָמִ֑ים וְאַתָּ֖ה פֹּ֥ה עֲמֹֽד

verses.restored: Amasa went to summon Judah, but delayed beyond appointed time set for him.

familiar.text: So Amasa went to assemble the men of Judah: but he tarried longer than the set time which he had appointed him.

modern.text: So Amasa went to summon Judah, but he took longer than the time allotted him.

original.text: וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ עֲמָשָׂ֖א לְהַזְעִ֣יק אֶת יְהוּדָ֑ה וייחר מִן הַמּוֹעֵ֖ד אֲשֶׁ֥ר יְעָדֽוֹ

verses.restored: David said to Abishai, Now Sheba son of Bichri will do us more evil than Absalom. Take servants of your lord and pursue him, lest he find fortified cities and escape our eyes.

familiar.text: And David said to Abishai, Now shall Sheba the son of Bichri do us more harm than did Absalom: take thou thy lord’s servants, and pursue after him, lest he get him fenced cities, and escape us.

modern.text: And David said to Abishai, “Now Sheba the son of Bichri will do us more harm than Absalom. Take your lord’s servants and pursue him, or he will find fortified cities and elude us. ”

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר דָּוִד֙ אֶל אֲבִישַׁ֔י עַתָּ֗ה יֵ֧רַֽע לָ֛נוּ שֶׁ֥בַע בֶּן בִּכְרִ֖י מִן אַבְשָׁל֑וֹם אַ֠תָּה קַ֞ח אֶת עַבְדֵ֤י אֲדֹנֶ֨יךָ֙ וּרְדֹ֣ף אַחֲרָ֔יו פֶּן מָ֥צָא ל֛וֹ עָרִ֥ים בְּצֻר֖וֹת וְהִצִּ֥יל עֵינֵֽנוּ

verses.restored: Men of Joab went out after him, with Cherethites, Pelethites, and all mighty warriors. They went out from Jerusalem to pursue Sheba son of Bichri.

familiar.text: And there went out after him Joab’s men, and the Cherethites, and the Pelethites, and all the mighty men: and they went out of Jerusalem, to pursue after Sheba the son of Bichri.

modern.text: So Joab’s men, along with the Cherethites, the Pelethites, and all the mighty men, marched out of Jerusalem in pursuit of Sheba son of Bichri.

original.text: וַיֵּצְא֤וּ אַֽחֲרָיו֙ אַנְשֵׁ֣י יוֹאָ֔ב וְהַכְּרֵתִ֥י וְהַפְּלֵתִ֖י וְכָל הַגִּבֹּרִ֑ים וַיֵּֽצְאוּ֙ מִיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם לִרְדֹּ֕ף אַחֲרֵ֖י שֶׁ֥בַע בֶּן בִּכְרִֽי

verses.restored: They were near great stone at Gibeon when Amasa came before them. Joab wore military garment, and upon it a belt with sword fastened at his waist in its sheath. As he went forward it fell/came out.

familiar.text: When they were at the great stone which is in Gibeon, Amasa went before them. And Joab’s garment that he had put on was girded unto him, and upon it a girdle with a sword fastened upon his loins in the sheath thereof; and as he went forth it fell out.

modern.text: And while they were at the great stone in Gibeon, Amasa joined them. Now Joab was dressed in military attire, with a dagger strapped to his belt. And as he stepped forward, he slipped the dagger from its sheath.

original.text: הֵ֗ם עִם הָאֶ֤בֶן הַגְּדוֹלָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּגִבְע֔וֹן וַעֲמָשָׂ֖א בָּ֣א לִפְנֵיהֶ֑ם וְיוֹאָ֞ב חָג֣וּר מִדּ֣וֹ לְבֻשׁ֗וּ ועלו חֲג֥וֹר חֶ֨רֶב֙ מְצֻמֶּ֤דֶת עַל מָתְנָיו֙ בְּתַעְרָ֔הּ וְה֥וּא יָצָ֖א וַתִּפֹּֽל

verses.restored: Joab said to Amasa, Is it peace with you, my brother? Joab took Amasa by beard with his right hand to kiss him.

familiar.text: And Joab said to Amasa, Art thou in health, my brother? And Joab took Amasa by the beard with the right hand to kiss him.

modern.text: “Are you well, my brother?” Joab asked Amasa. And with his right hand Joab grabbed Amasa by the beard to kiss him.

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יוֹאָב֙ לַעֲמָשָׂ֔א הֲשָׁל֥וֹם אַתָּ֖ה אָחִ֑י וַתֹּ֜חֶז יַד יְמִ֥ין יוֹאָ֛ב בִּזְקַ֥ן עֲמָשָׂ֖א לִנְשָׁק לֽוֹ

verses.restored: Amasa did not guard himself from sword in Joab's hand. Joab struck him in belly, spilling his inward parts to ground; he did not strike him again, and he died. Joab and Abishai his brother pursued Sheba son of Bichri.

familiar.text: But Amasa took no heed to the sword that was in Joab’s hand: so he smote him therewith in the fifth rib, and shed out his bowels to the ground, and struck him not again; and he died. So Joab and Abishai his brother pursued after Sheba the son of Bichri.

modern.text: Amasa was not on guard against the dagger in Joab’s hand, and Joab stabbed him in the stomach and spilled out his intestines on the ground. And Joab did not need to strike him again, for Amasa was dead. Then Joab and his brother Abishai pursued Sheba son of Bichri.

original.text: וַעֲמָשָׂ֨א לֹֽא נִשְׁמַ֜ר בַּחֶ֣רֶב אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּיַד יוֹאָ֗ב וַיַּכֵּהוּ֩ בָ֨הּ אֶל הַחֹ֜מֶשׁ וַיִּשְׁפֹּ֨ךְ מֵעָ֥יו אַ֛רְצָה וְלֹא שָׁ֥נָה ל֖וֹ וַיָּמֹ֑ת וְיוֹאָב֙ וַאֲבִישַׁ֣י אָחִ֔יו רָדַ֕ף אַחֲרֵ֖י שֶׁ֥בַע בֶּן בִּכְרִֽי

verses.restored: One of Joab's young men stood beside him and said, Whoever delights in Joab and whoever is for David, after Joab.

familiar.text: And one of Joab’s men stood by him, and said, He that favoureth Joab, and he that is for David, let him go after Joab.

modern.text: One of Joab’s young men stood near Amasa and said, “Whoever favors Joab, and whoever is for David, let him follow Joab!”

original.text: וְאִישׁ֙ עָמַ֣ד עָלָ֔יו מִֽנַּעֲרֵ֖י יוֹאָ֑ב וַיֹּ֗אמֶר מִי֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר חָפֵ֧ץ בְּיוֹאָ֛ב וּמִ֥י אֲשֶׁר לְדָוִ֖ד אַחֲרֵ֥י יוֹאָֽב

verses.restored: Amasa was wallowing in blood in middle of highway. Man saw all people stood still. He moved Amasa from highway to field and threw garment over him when he saw everyone coming to him stood still.

familiar.text: And Amasa wallowed in blood in the midst of the highway. And when the man saw that all the people stood still, he removed Amasa out of the highway into the field, and cast a cloth upon him, when he saw that every one that came by him stood still.

modern.text: But Amasa wallowed in his blood in the middle of the road, and when the man saw that all the troops were stopping there, he dragged the body off the road into a field and threw a garment over it.

original.text: וַעֲמָשָׂ֛א מִתְגֹּלֵ֥ל בַּדָּ֖ם בְּת֣וֹךְ הַֽמְסִּלָּ֑ה וַיַּ֨רְא הָאִ֜ישׁ כִּֽי עָמַ֣ד כָּל הָעָ֗ם וַיַּסֵּב֩ אֶת עֲמָשָׂ֨א מִן הַֽמְסִלָּ֤ה הַשָּׂדֶה֙ וַיַּשְׁלֵ֤ךְ עָלָיו֙ בֶּ֔גֶד כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר רָאָ֔ה כָּל הַבָּ֥א עָלָ֖יו וְעָמָֽד

verses.restored: When he was removed from highway, every man passed after Joab to pursue Sheba son of Bichri.

familiar.text: When he was removed out of the highway, all the people went on after Joab, to pursue after Sheba the son of Bichri.

modern.text: As soon as Amasa’s body was removed from the road, all the men went on with Joab to pursue Sheba son of Bichri.

original.text: כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר הֹגָ֖ה מִן הַֽמְסִלָּ֑ה עָבַ֤ר כָּל אִישׁ֙ אַחֲרֵ֣י יוֹאָ֔ב לִרְדֹּ֕ף אַחֲרֵ֖י שֶׁ֥בַע בֶּן בִּכְרִֽי

verses.restored: Sheba passed through all tribes of Israel to Abel, Beth-maacah, and all Berites. They gathered and also came after him.

familiar.text: And he went through all the tribes of Israel unto Abel, and to Bethmaachah, and all the Berites: and they were gathered together, and went also after him.

modern.text: Sheba passed through all the tribes of Israel to Abel-beth-maacah and through the entire region of the Berites, who gathered together and followed him.

original.text: וַֽיַּעֲבֹ֞ר בְּכָל שִׁבְטֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל אָבֵ֛לָה וּבֵ֥ית מַעֲכָ֖ה וְכָל הַבֵּרִ֑ים ויקלהו וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ אַף אַחֲרָֽיו

verses.restored: They came and besieged him in Abel Beth-maacah. They poured up siege mound against city, standing at rampart, and all people with Joab were destroying wall to cause it to fall.

familiar.text: And they came and besieged him in Abel of Bethmaachah, and they cast up a bank against the city, and it stood in the trench: and all the people that were with Joab battered the wall, to throw it down.

modern.text: And Joab’s troops came and besieged Sheba in Abel-beth-maacah and built a siege ramp against the outer rampart of the city. As all the troops with Joab were battering the wall to topple it,

original.text: וַיָּבֹ֜אוּ וַיָּצֻ֣רוּ עָלָ֗יו בְּאָבֵ֨לָה֙ בֵּ֣ית הַֽמַּעֲכָ֔ה וַיִּשְׁפְּכ֤וּ סֹֽלְלָה֙ אֶל הָעִ֔יר וַֽתַּעֲמֹ֖ד בַּחֵ֑ל וְכָל הָעָם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֶת יוֹאָ֔ב מַשְׁחִיתִ֖ם לְהַפִּ֥יל הַחוֹמָֽה

verses.restored: A wise woman called from city, Hear, hear. Please say to Joab, Come near here, that I may speak with you.

familiar.text: Then cried a wise woman out of the city, Hear, hear; say, I pray you, unto Joab, Come near hither, that I may speak with thee.

modern.text: a wise woman called out from the city, “Listen! Listen! Please tell Joab to come here so that I may speak with him.”

original.text: וַתִּקְרָ֛א אִשָּׁ֥ה חֲכָמָ֖ה מִן הָעִ֑יר שִׁמְע֤וּ שִׁמְעוּ֙ אִמְרוּ נָ֣א אֶל יוֹאָ֔ב קְרַ֣ב עַד הֵ֔נָּה וַאֲדַבְּרָ֖ה אֵלֶֽיךָ

verses.restored: He came near to her. Woman said, Are you Joab? He said, I am. She said, Hear words of your maidservant. He said, I hear.

familiar.text: And when he was come near unto her, the woman said, Art thou Joab? And he answered, I am he. Then she said unto him, Hear the words of thine handmaid. And he answered, I do hear.

modern.text: When he had come near to her, the woman asked, “Are you Joab?” “I am,” he replied. “Listen to the words of your servant,” she said. “I am listening,” he answered.

original.text: וַיִּקְרַ֣ב אֵלֶ֔יהָ וַתֹּ֧אמֶר הָאִשָּׁ֛ה הַאַתָּ֥ה יוֹאָ֖ב וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אָ֑נִי וַתֹּ֣אמֶר ל֗וֹ שְׁמַע֙ דִּבְרֵ֣י אֲמָתֶ֔ךָ וַיֹּ֖אמֶר שֹׁמֵ֥עַ אָנֹֽכִי

verses.restored: She spoke, saying, Speaking, they used to speak in former time, saying, Let them surely inquire at Abel; thus they completed matters.

familiar.text: Then she spake, saying, They were wont to speak in old time, saying, They shall surely ask counsel at Abel: and so they ended the matter.

modern.text: Then the woman said, “Long ago they used to say, ‘Seek counsel at Abel,’ and that is how disputes were settled.

original.text: וַתֹּ֖אמֶר לֵאמֹ֑ר דַּבֵּ֨ר יְדַבְּר֤וּ בָרִֽאשֹׁנָה֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר שָׁאֹ֧ל יְשָׁאֲל֛וּ בְּאָבֵ֖ל וְכֵ֥ן הֵתַֽמּוּ

verses.restored: I am among peaceful and faithful of Israel. You seek to put to death a city and a mother in Israel. Why will you swallow inheritance of YHWH?

familiar.text: I am one of them that are peaceable and faithful in Israel: thou seekest to destroy a city and a mother in Israel: why wilt thou swallow up the inheritance of the LORD?

modern.text: I am among the peaceable and faithful in Israel, but you are trying to destroy a city that is a mother in Israel. Why would you swallow up the LORD’s inheritance?”

original.text: אָנֹכִ֕י שְׁלֻמֵ֖י אֱמוּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אַתָּ֣ה מְבַקֵּ֗שׁ לְהָמִ֨ית עִ֤יר וְאֵם֙ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לָ֥מָּה תְבַלַּ֖ע נַחֲלַ֥ת יְהוָֽה

verses.restored: Joab answered and said, Far be it, far be it from me, that I should swallow or destroy.

familiar.text: And Joab answered and said, Far be it, far be it from me, that I should swallow up or destroy.

modern.text: “Far be it!” Joab declared. “Far be it from me to swallow up or destroy!

original.text: וַיַּ֥עַן יוֹאָ֖ב וַיֹּאמַ֑ר חָלִ֤ילָה חָלִ֨ילָה֙ לִ֔י אִם אֲבַלַּ֖ע וְאִם אַשְׁחִֽית

verses.restored: Matter is not so. A man from hill country of Ephraim, Sheba son of Bichri his name, lifted his hand against king, against David. Give him alone, and I will go from city. Woman said to Joab, Look, his head will be thrown to you over wall.

familiar.text: The matter is not so: but a man of mount Ephraim, Sheba the son of Bichri by name, hath lifted up his hand against the king, even against David: deliver him only, and I will depart from the city. And the woman said unto Joab, Behold, his head shall be thrown to thee over the wall.

modern.text: That is not the case. But a man named Sheba son of Bichri, from the hill country of Ephraim, has lifted up his hand against the king, against David. Deliver him alone, and I will depart from the city.” “Look,” the woman replied, “his head will be thrown to you over the wall.”

original.text: לֹא כֵ֣ן הַדָּבָ֗ר כִּ֡י אִישׁ֩ מֵהַ֨ר אֶפְרַ֜יִם שֶׁ֧בַע בֶּן בִּכְרִ֣י שְׁמ֗וֹ נָשָׂ֤א יָדוֹ֙ בַּמֶּ֣לֶךְ בְּדָוִ֔ד תְּנֽוּ אֹת֣וֹ לְבַדּ֔וֹ וְאֵלְכָ֖ה מֵעַ֣ל הָעִ֑יר וַתֹּ֤אמֶר הָֽאִשָּׁה֙ אֶל יוֹאָ֔ב הִנֵּ֥ה רֹאשׁ֛וֹ מֻשְׁלָ֥ךְ אֵלֶ֖יךָ בְּעַ֥ד הַחוֹמָֽה

verses.restored: Woman came to all people in her wisdom. They cut off head of Sheba son of Bichri and threw it to Joab. He blew shofar; they scattered from city, each to his tent. Joab returned to Jerusalem to king.

familiar.text: Then the woman went unto all the people in her wisdom. And they cut off the head of Sheba the son of Bichri, and cast it out to Joab. And he blew a trumpet, and they retired from the city, every man to his tent. And Joab returned to Jerusalem unto the king.

modern.text: Then the woman went to all the people with her wise counsel, and they cut off the head of Sheba son of Bichri and threw it to Joab. So he blew the ram’s horn and his men dispersed from the city, each to his own home. And Joab returned to the king in Jerusalem.

translation_notes: The ten concubines were raped publicly in chapter 16 after David left them behind. He now confines them for life, provides food, and withdraws sexual access. This is not survivor-centered care, freedom, justice, or chosen widowhood.
Their confinement protects royal honor and controls dynastic sexuality. The women receive no recorded hearing, compensation, household autonomy, or choice of future.
Joab greets Amasa as 'my brother,' takes his beard as if to kiss him, and murders him. Intimate gestures can be weaponized by violent officials.
Amasa's exposed body stops the army until it is moved and covered. The corpse is treated as an operational obstruction after command assassination.
The soldier's cry merges loyalty to Joab with loyalty to David, demonstrating how an unauthorized commander can capture institutional allegiance through violence.
Joab threatens an entire city for one fugitive. Siege warfare places civilians, food, homes, and a 'mother in Israel' under collective danger.
The wise woman saves the city through negotiation, but the outcome is summary beheading without a recorded trial. Collective survival under siege constrains meaningful consent.
Joab denies wanting destruction while actively battering the wall; stated intent must be tested against actual methods.
The administrative list includes forced labor/tribute. Restored royal order still rests upon coercive extraction.
safety_note: Do not call the ten women's lifelong confinement compassionate, excuse Joab's murder as efficiency, or praise Sheba's beheading as clean justice. Center survivors' autonomy, due process, civilian protection, and the wise woman's challenge: no ruler may swallow a whole community to reach one opponent.
